settings.description: The knowledge store Keystone remembers in. With none, Keystone keeps your chats and remembers nothing between them. The built-in store keeps what it remembers in your own Keystone folder. Waymarks is your own Waymarks instance, at the address and with the tokens you give.
Where your Waymarks instance is, such as http://127.0.0.1:7878. Its tokens are kept with your secrets and never here.
How long Keystone waits for one answer from Waymarks before it carries on without it, from 100ms to 2m.
The most results one search of Waymarks returns when the search names no limit, from 1 to 100.
The most pages Keystone asks Waymarks for at once when it lists the pages needing a vector, from 1 to 1000.
The largest answer Keystone reads from Waymarks, in megabytes, from 1 to 1024. A larger one is treated as Waymarks being unavailable.
The most results one search of the built-in knowledge store returns when the search names no limit, from 1 to 1000.
About how many words of a matching page or source a result from the built-in knowledge store shows, from 1 to 64.
The most pages the built-in knowledge store lists at once as needing a vector, from 1 to 10000.
The longest a person's profile may be, in characters, from 1 to 20000. The profile starts every call to a model, so a longer one costs more on every message.

The most room the map of your knowledge store may take at the start of a call, in tokens, from 0 to 20000. A map that would be larger shows fewer titles, then fewer kinds of page, then fewer spaces. With 0 no map is sent.
How many page titles the map of your knowledge store shows under each kind of page, from 0 to 20. With 0 it shows the kinds and their counts alone.
The longest a space's name, a kind of page or a page title is shown in the map of a knowledge store, in characters, from 8 to 200. A longer one is cut.
Whether Keystone searches your knowledge store with each message you send and gives the model what it finds. With no knowledge store nothing is searched either way.
How long recall may take before a reply starts without it, from 100ms to 1m. A knowledge store that is slow or down never stops a chat.

The relevance threshold for recall from the built-in knowledge store. A page or source that scores lower for your message is left out. The score is the store's own ranking: in a store of a few dozen pages or more, a word that few pages hold scores about 1 or more, and a word that half the pages hold scores close to 0. With 0 everything the search finds may be recalled, which is right for a small store.

The relevance threshold for recall from Waymarks. A page or source that scores lower for your message is left out. The score is on Waymarks' own scale. With 0 everything the search finds may be recalled.

settings.description: Words recall leaves out when it searches your knowledge store with a message, separated by spaces. They are words that say nothing of what a message is about. A message made of them alone recalls nothing.
The most results recall asks your knowledge store for with each message, from 1 to 100, before the relevance threshold is applied.
The most pages and sources recall gives the model with one message, from 0 to 50. With 0 nothing is recalled.
The most of one recalled page or source the model is given, in characters, from 100 to 100000. A longer one is cut, and the model can read the rest with a lookup.
The most of your message recall searches with, in characters from its start, from 1 to 10000.

settings.default: This person keeps a knowledge store of their own. Before you answer anything about their world, or say you do not know, look in it. What Keystone found there for this message is given further down, when it found anything. When knowledge lookup tools are offered, search with them and read a page or a source in full. Say which page or source an answer came from.
settings.description: The search-first rule: what the standing instructions tell the model when you have a knowledge store. It is left out when you have none. Empty sends none.

The memory pass: after each reply, a model reads what you wrote and the answer, and adds the durable facts it finds to your knowledge store, as a source that points back to the chat. It runs only when your store can take new sources, never in an incognito chat, and never delays a reply.
The space in your knowledge store the memory pass puts facts in. A space your store does not have yet is made, as a normal space.

The space the memory pass puts facts in when the chat was sent content from a sensitive space. Your store must already have it, with a page in it, and say it is sensitive. Empty keeps such facts nowhere.

The most the memory pass may spend in a calendar month on models that are not local, in US dollars. It is part of the monthly cap, not added to it, so the memory pass stops before it eats the cap. A local model costs nothing and is never stopped. Zero keeps the memory pass to local models.

settings.default: You keep the long-term memory of a personal assistant. You are shown one exchange from a chat: what the person wrote and what the assistant answered. Write down the durable facts it shows about the person and their world: who they are, the people, places and things in their life, their projects, plans, habits, preferences and decisions, when they will still be true and useful in a later chat. Leave out what matters only to this conversation, what the assistant suggested that the person did not take up, general knowledge, and anything you are not sure of. Write each fact as one short sentence that stands on its own, and call the person "the person". Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form: {"facts": ["...", "..."]}. Write at most {max} facts. When the exchange holds no durable fact, answer {"facts": []}.
settings.description: The instruction the memory pass's model is given with each exchange. {max} becomes the most facts it may write. The answer must stay one JSON object with a list of facts.
The name of the source the memory pass adds for one reply. {title} becomes the chat's title and {date} the day of the reply.
The most facts the memory pass keeps from one reply, from 1 to 100.
The longest fact the memory pass keeps, in characters, from 20 to 2000. A longer one is left out.
The most of your message, and of the reply, the memory pass's model is shown, in characters, from 200 to 100000. A longer one is cut at a word's end.
The longest answer the memory pass's model may write, in tokens, from 64 to 32000.
How long one memory pass may take, its model call included, from 5s to 30m. A pass that runs out of time keeps nothing and says so in the server's log.

How long an incognito chat you have not left is kept once nothing more is said in it, from 5m to 720h. Then it is deleted with its messages, as it is at once when you leave it. Its model calls stay in the audit log, as every call does.
How often Keystone looks for incognito chats to delete: those you left, and those idle for longer than knowledge.incognito_keep. From 5s to 1h.
The most sources the memory pass added that the Memory screen shows, the newest first, from 1 to 5000.
The most pages of each space the Memory screen lists, from 0 to 1000. The rest are counted.
The most results one knowledge search by the model returns, from 1 to 100.
The most text one knowledge lookup by the model returns, in characters, from 200 to 200000. A longer page or source is read in parts.
